steps.title: Shiraz
steps.body: Shiraz, Syrah, is the Barossa's signature, about half of the vineyards. It gives full-bodied, ripe wines with blackberry, plum, chocolate, liquorice and spice, often 14.5 to 15% alcohol, with soft, ripe tannins. Traditional examples use American oak, adding vanilla and coconut. Penfolds Grange, first made in 1951, often includes Barossa Shiraz.
steps.highlight: Rich Shiraz, about half the vines

steps.title: Grenache and Mourvèdre
steps.body: Grenache, often from old bush vines, gives red fruit and spice. Mourvèdre, called Mataro locally, adds tannin and savoury notes. Blends of Grenache, Shiraz and Mourvèdre, GSM, are a Barossa classic. Cabernet Sauvignon and Semillon also grow. Eden Valley adds Riesling.

steps.prompt: Match each grape to its role.

steps.body: Mataro, the Barossa's name for Mourvèdre, comes from the town of Mataró near Barcelona.

steps.prompt: What is Barossa Shiraz typically like?

steps.title: What you learned
points: Shiraz is the Barossa's signature, rich and ripe
Grenache and Mataro join it in GSM blends
Penfolds Grange often includes Barossa Shiraz
